frequency_question: How often do nations successfully establish operational domestic production lines for complex guided missiles within a 24-month window when facing severe infrastructure and technical friction?
membership_rule: Members are programs initiated to stand up domestic manufacturing or final assembly lines for advanced guided munitions (cruise missiles, air defense systems, precision-guided rockets) within a 2-year crisis window by nations lacking prior indigenous production of that specific class. Excluded are simple unguided munitions, routine ammunition lines, and programs with unlimited timelines (>5 years).

cases.name: UK wartime Shadow factory program (aircraft/munitions localization, 1940-1941)
Soviet Ural tank and artillery factory evacuation and relaunch (1941-1942)
Taiwan Hsiung Feng II/III missile domestic production scaling (1980s crisis periods)
Pakistan Hatf/Shaheen missile indigenous manufacturing setup (1990s)
Iran domestic surface-to-air and cruise missile reverse-engineering/production (2000-2005)
South Korea K-2/Chunmoo rapid localized defense manufacturing surge (2010s)
Ukraine Neptune anti-ship missile serial production establishment (2018-2021)
Ukraine Stugna-P rapid wartime scale-up and decentralized production (2022-2024)

provenance_note: claimed 6 hits but 7 of 8 cases are marked hit; rate recomputed from the cases
coverage_note: 8 named; representative of major historical and modern state-level rapid missile/weapon system industrial localization efforts under extreme friction.
known_gaps: Classified bilateral assistance programs in recent decades that lack fully public verification.
skeleton: 8 historical crisis-driven defense localization programs across major conflict or embargo periods, tracking whether operational production/assembly was achieved within the target window.
validity_reason: Industrial manufacturing base constraints, engineering bottlenecks, and supply chain friction constants change slowly over decades.
